question: How does nanoscale confinement affect the adsorption selectivity of methane-ethane mixtures in shale pores?
answer: Nanoscale confinement within shale pores enhances the selective adsorption of ethane over methane.  This selectivity diminishes with increasing temperature and pore size, approaching unity as pore size increases and confined fluid composition matches the bulk composition.  Confinement also alters phase behavior, decreasing critical pressure and temperature compared to bulk mixtures, and shifting dew and bubble point pressures. This preferential adsorption of heavier components within the shale can lead to compositional variations in produced fluids over time.

### Task 1: Summary of the Purpose of the Paper  
The paper aims to investigate the behavior of hydrocarbon mixtures (specifically methane-ethane) in nanoscale confined environments, such as shale reservoir pores, using molecular simulations. It focuses on understanding how confinement alters fluid properties, adsorption selectivity, and phase equilibria compared to bulk systems. The research uses molecular dynamics (MD) and grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations to model kerogen pores and explore the effects of pore size, temperature, and pressure on fluid behavior.
